While the story convincingly and deeply explores the morally objectionable mindset of its protagonist, Ruth—who knowingly decides to keep a healthy baby that was accidentally switched with her own premature infant—it does not provide diverse perspectives. The narrative is told entirely from Ruth's close third-person point of view. Other characters, such as her husband Paul, the hospital staff, and the other mothers in the ward (including the real mother of the baby, Mrs. Lindqvist), are only observed externally or imagined by Ruth, rather than having their own viewpoints depicted.
